## How they got there
Inter finished as runner-up after losing the final to Manchester City 0-1. Their profile during the group and league phases was defined by high shot accuracy at 59.3, which placed them better than 97% of teams, followed by a shot conversion rate of 18.5 that beat 62% of peers, and a long pass percentage of 12.9 where they outperformed 62% of the season's participants.

## Would the model have picked them?
With a model probability of just 2.9%, significantly lower than the 12.5% base rate for reaching the final, Inter ranked only 14th among all knockout teams in that season. Because this rank falls well below the top two required for the model to select a finalist, it did not pick them despite their actual run to the last game. The model's expected stage was calculated at 0.09, which corresponds nearest to being out before quarter-finals rather than reaching the final.

## Weak spots
The team's weakest statistical areas were passes per game at 470 and opponent shots on target per game at 5.7, where they beat fewer opponents than in their top metrics. Although the model marked attacks per game down with a negative contribution of -0.22, Inter still ranked better than 42% of teams on that stat. Similarly, while goal difference per game carried a negative weight, the club was superior to 61% of its peers, indicating no single clear weakness dominated their performance profile.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
